item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"ARC-AGI-2 supports comparisons of success on unfamiliar grid transformations under specified evaluation conditions. Its example-based tasks, review for repeated rules and separation of development from evaluation support the intended focus on inferring rules. Human difficulty matching supports the construction of the three test sets, but does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI systems. Exact matching makes answer correctness explicit, while the inspected software awards partial problem credit when only some new inputs are solved. Scores therefore need to be distinguished from percentages of fully solved problems. Verified settings and spending limits aid comparison, but single runs, unresolved exposure and absent estimates of score variation limit confidence in small differences. Public materials and revision records support inspection, although affected historical scores are not all recalculated. The evidence supports conclusions about grid-task performance; broader reasoning and intelligence claims remain unresolved.","supported_claims":["The benchmark tests whether systems can produce correct outputs for grid transformations inferred from examples.","The inspected software averages within-problem fractions of correctly answered inputs, allowing two attempts per input.","Human solving results informed test selection and matching for human difficulty.","Verified evaluations specify settings and spending limits, and public materials permit inspection of tasks and scoring."],"documented_problems":["The software's fractional problem scores differ from the dataset's definition of a fully solved problem.","Post-release corrections addressed coloured squares and unclear examples; affected AI scores are not all recalculated.","Verified testing uses one run, and public evaluation problems are accessible to anyone.","Exposure protections for hidden tests acknowledge that information could still escape."],"missing_information":["Repeated identical-test results and uncertainty estimates for AI scores.","Systematic evidence about effects of instructions, grid presentation and software settings.","Evidence that matching human difficulty also makes the test sets comparable for AI systems.","Independent validation of the complete marking system and verification of the complete reporting archive.","Evidence connecting scores to performance beyond two-dimensional grid tasks, and evidence excluding unintended routes to high scores."],"reinterpretations":["For AI, human-matched difficulty is a test-construction feature, not an established measure of AI difficulty.","A score measures exact output success within the permitted attempts and evaluation conditions; it does not identify the reasoning process used.","A fractional average problem score is not the proportion of problems fully solved.","A verified result describes a configured system under a spending limit, rather than a condition-independent measure of intelligence."],"closing_note":"Reports should clarify whether 'solved' means fully solved problems or fractional software credit. The boundary between allowed development and discouraged evaluation-specific changes is not fully specified in the supplied passage."},{"benchmark":"designqa","instrument_review":"DesignQA provides a practical, bounded assessment of answering questions about Formula SAE rules and vehicle materials. Its six task groups cover several relevant activities, but one rulebook and uneven group sizes limit coverage of engineering work. Practitioner input and additional review support question relevance, while incomplete review coverage and unreported disagreement leave answer quality uncertain. Scoring mixes text similarity and decision accuracy; documented sensitivity to formatting and omitted valid rules weakens interpretation as engineering understanding. Equal weighting of the six groups defines a particular summary, without establishing a common underlying skill. Comparisons also depend on information supply because systems receive different rulebook contexts. Small groups, insufficient uncertainty information and incomplete historical records limit fine rankings and reproducibility. The results support task-specific comparisons under documented conditions, with broader engineering competence remaining unestablished.","supported_claims":["The benchmark contains 1,451 question-and-answer pairs across six groups using real competition rules and vehicle materials.","The tasks examine rule retrieval, terminology, component identification, dimensions and functional requirements.","The paper describes tested systems, instructions and settings, and examines several changes to supplied information and images.","Public questions, scoring code, instructions and some responses support partial inspection of results."],"documented_problems":["Coverage is limited to one rulebook and a narrow task range, with 1,192 individual-rule questions but only 16 performance reference answers.","Systems receive different information supplies, complicating direct model comparisons.","All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes response to earn decision credit on that portion.","Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to results, and one answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding reported question count."],"missing_information":["Reviewer disagreement rates, remaining answer errors and comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency evidence.","Evidence validating group scores or the equally baseline and evidence of transfer to other documents or engineering projects.","A protected evaluation set, systematic exposure checks and clear rules for training on questions or repeated correctness alone.","Equal group weighting gives each task group the same influence despite different sizes and marking methods; it does not establish balanced engineering competence.","Correct yes/no answers on uniformly compliant drawings do not by themselves demonstrate rule application.","Variation across different retrieved passages measures sensitivity to supplied information, not repeatability under identical conditions."],"closing_note":"The supplied material leaves acceptance of alternative correct wording or rules insufficiently clear.
